summary.text: The council maps shallow landslide susceptibility as Very Low, large-scale susceptibility as Low, and liquefaction vulnerability as Unlikely here; its landslide ratings do not measure risk for an individual property.
The debt-to-income ratio (DTI) assessment assumes no existing debts because that input was not provided.

The property record identifies a Unit Title; Settled.govt.nz says ownership automatically includes body corporate membership, and the government unit titles guide says owners pay levies for operation and maintenance.

Based on what you told us, your supplied build year differs from the property record, so the recorded 1990 build-decade value takes precedence and places the property in the era discussed by Settled.govt.nz in its leaky-buildings guidance.
Based on what you told us, the cladding is monolithic, which Settled.govt.nz discusses in its leaky-buildings guidance; the public property data could not verify the cladding.

next_steps.text: Check the council property file for geotechnical reports, or ask a geotechnical engineer for site-specific advice.
Request the body corporate rules, meeting minutes, maintenance plan and levy details.
Ask your lawyer for the body corporate's current levy amounts, budget and long-term maintenance plan.
Ask for the building's age and cladding details and consider a pre-purchase building inspection.
Ask whether the cladding is monolithic and consider a pre-purchase building inspection.
Ask for the body corporate insurance policy and check whether you need separate cover for your unit and contents.
